components-globalerrorfallback--docs.title: Components/GlobalErrorFallback
components-globalerrorfallback--docs.content:
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';

<Meta title="Components/GlobalErrorFallback" />

# GlobalErrorFallback

Use `GlobalErrorFallback` as a full-page error message, for example as an
`ErrorBoundary` fallback.

```tsx
import { ErrorBoundary, GlobalErrorFallback } from '@a-type/ui';

<ErrorBoundary fallback={<GlobalErrorFallback />}>
	<App />
</ErrorBoundary>;
```

It includes a refresh button and changes its message after a recent refresh
attempt. Pass children to include actions such as a bug-report link. The
`ReloadButton` is also exported for use on its own.

components-navbar--docs.name: Docs
components-navbar--docs.title: Components/NavBar
components-navbar--docs.content:
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';

<Meta title="Components/NavBar" />

# NavBar

Compose a navigation bar from `NavBar` and its item parts.

```tsx
import { NavBar } from '@a-type/ui';

<nav aria-label="Primary">
	<NavBar>
		<NavBar.Item
			active
			render={<a href="/" aria-current="page" />}
			nativeButton={false}
		>
			<NavBar.ItemIcon name="home" />
			<NavBar.ItemText>Home</NavBar.ItemText>
		</NavBar.Item>
	</NavBar>
</nav>;
```

`active` changes the item's appearance; routing and the current-page state are
the caller's responsibility. `NavBar.ItemPip` can display a notification marker.
Use `PageNav` to place the bar in the page layout.

components-provider--docs.name: Docs
components-provider--docs.title: Components/Provider
components-provider--docs.content:
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';

<Meta title="Components/Provider" />

# Provider

Import the library stylesheet and wrap your application in `Provider`.

```tsx
import '@a-type/ui/main.css';
import { Provider } from '@a-type/ui';

<Provider>
	<App />
</Provider>;
```

The provider supplies the icon spritesheet, toast and tooltip providers,
particle layer, and PWA install dialog. It also manages viewport and virtual
keyboard behavior.

- The install dialog loads `/manifest.json` by default. Pass `manifestPath` to
  change the path, or `manifestPath={false}` to disable the dialog.
- `disableParticles` omits the particle layer. Otherwise, its children render
  after the client mounts.
- `virtualKeyboardBehavior` accepts `displace` (the default) or `overlay` on
  supported browsers. `disableViewportOffset` and `disableTitleBarColor` opt
  out of those global updates.

components-hidewhilekeyboardopen--docs.content:
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';

<Meta title="Components/HideWhileKeyboardOpen" />

# HideWhileKeyboardOpen

Wrap content that should be hidden while the on-screen keyboard is open.

```tsx
import { HideWhileKeyboardOpen } from '@a-type/ui';

<HideWhileKeyboardOpen>
	<nav aria-label="Primary">Navigation</nav>
</HideWhileKeyboardOpen>;
```

It uses the configured virtual-keyboard behavior and a viewport-size heuristic
where appropriate, so detection depends on browser support. `PageNav` uses this
component automatically.

components-slotdiv--docs.content:
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';

<Meta title="Components/SlotDiv" />

# SlotDiv

`SlotDiv` renders a `div` by default and can render another element through the
Base UI `render` prop.

```tsx
import { SlotDiv } from '@a-type/ui';

<SlotDiv render={<a href="/settings" />}>Settings</SlotDiv>;
```

Props and the ref are merged into the rendered element. Components such as
`Box` build on the same pattern.
